title: Being A Peacemaker
subtitle: Making peace is work. Avoiding conflict is not the same thing.
objectives: Distinguish making peace from avoiding conflict

cards.title: A peacemaker is not someone who avoids conflict
cards.text: Matthew 5:9 says blessed are the peacemakers — the ones who make it. Making something takes work, and usually a conversation nobody wants.

cards.title: Two different things
cards.text: They look similar from the outside and are opposites underneath.
points: **Avoiding conflict** leaves the problem running.
**Making peace** deals with it, which is uncomfortable.
**Keeping quiet is cheaper** in the short term.
**And it is not what the verse says.**

cards.title: You walk the steps
cards.text: Pick the first step. Each other route shows what it would cost.

question.text: Matthew 18 says the first step is to…
question.explain: As privately as possible, so backing down stays cheap.

cards.title: Smallest first, widening only when it must
cards.text: The sequence is designed, not arbitrary.
points: **Alone** — nobody has to lose face.
**Then one or two others** — the smallest help that could work.
**Then the wider body** — only if the first two failed.
**Going public first** removes everyone's way out.

question.text: Why does the sequence start privately?
options: Backing down stays cheap when nobody is watching
question.explain: An audience makes retreat expensive for everyone.

cards.title: One on tone, one on limits
cards.text: Both are practical rather than abstract.
points: **Proverbs 15:1:** a soft answer turns away wrath.
**Tone is a separate decision from content.**
**Romans 12:18:** *as far as it depends on you*, live at peace.
**That clause is a limit.** Some of it does not depend on you.

cards.title: Tone is a separate choice from content
cards.text: You can say a hard thing quietly, and the quiet is what lets it land.
points: **A coach can tell you your guard dropped** without shouting.
**Same information, different delivery.**
**Shouted, you defend yourself** instead of listening.
**Proverbs 15:1 is about delivery**, not softening the truth.

cards.title: Escalating straight to public is a mistake
cards.text: Everyone has seen a small thing become unfixable this way.
points: **One message privately** usually ends it.
**One post publicly** draws an audience and sides.
**Now nobody can apologise** without losing face.
**The order in Matthew 18 prevents exactly that.**

cards.title: Some of it does not depend on you
cards.text: Romans 12:18 contains a clause that protects you.
points: **You can do your part properly** and it still fails.
**That is not your failure.**
**You are responsible for your side** of it.
**Not for both sides.**

cards.title: What to remember
points: Peacemaking is work; avoiding conflict is not the same thing.
Matthew 18: alone, then one or two, then the wider body.
Proverbs 15:1 — a soft answer; tone is a separate decision.
Romans 12:18 — as far as it depends on you. That clause is a limit.

teacher.summary: Term 2 Week 9 Devotion. The distinction that carries the week is between making peace and avoiding conflict, which look alike from outside and are opposites underneath; Matthew 5:9 blesses the makers. The Matthew 18 sequence is walked as an interactive, with the design reason stated: starting privately keeps backing down cheap, and going public first removes everyone's way out. Two verses do practical work — Proverbs 15:1 separates tone from content, so a hard thing can be said quietly, and Romans 12:18's clause "as far as it depends on you" is given as a protective limit rather than a loophole.
discussion: Ask the difference between making peace and avoiding conflict.
Ask for the three steps, in order, and why that order.
Ask what Proverbs 15:1 is actually about.
Ask what the clause in Romans 12:18 protects him from.
extension: Have him resolve one real small thing by going to the person first.
Have him rewrite a hard sentence three times, same content, softer tone.
misconceptions: "A peacemaker keeps the peace by staying quiet." Making is work.
"A soft answer means not saying it." Tone, not content.
"If it is not resolved, I failed." As far as it depends on you.
